entryWatch.setup: MDT day-2 continuation after the 9/1 beat-and-raise - the name the 9/1 file flagged as worth this open's attention if it built a shelf. It built it. The 9/1 reaction bar opened 94.00, ran 95.41, flushed to 90.80 and closed 92.04 on 18.8M shares against roughly 6.5M typical - a faded gap that nonetheless HELD 1.53% above the 90.65 pre-print close, which is the exact line SAIC and NTNX failed. The afternoon based 92.24-92.96 for four hours. Today opened 91.47, below yesterday's close and below that base, held above the 90.80 reaction low, and reversed to a 93.39 high. SPECIFIED at 09:45 at a 93.07 limit for 4 shares, CLEAN, no checklist item marked fail, struck AT THE OFFER rather than under the bid as the direct correction to yesterday's DG failure.
entryWatch.trigger: LIVE SPECIFICATION, RE-QUOTED AND CONFIRMED FOR A SECOND HOUR AT 11:21 BY THE MID-SESSION RUN, expiring 15:30 ET today. MDT 94.16 bid / 94.20 ask at 2026-09-02T15:22:04.063978947Z, last 94.160, +2.30% against a 92.04 settled close, on a 0.04 spread that is 0.042% of mark. Limit 93.07 UNCHANGED AND NOT RAISED, target 111.68, stop 85.62, time stop the 9/9 close. ALL FOUR NAMED INVALIDATIONS RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE TAPE AND NONE FIRED: the session low is still 91.47, the opening print itself, and the name has never traded below it - every bar low since is 92.51 or higher and the bid is 2.86% clear of it; the 90.80 reaction low is 3.57% below the bid and was never approached; no close exists below 90.65 and the name is 3.51 above it; and MDT is +2.30% so it cannot close red on a green XLV day from here without a reversal. THE COUNTERWEIGHT STORY HAS PARTIALLY REVERTED AND IS RECORDED IN THAT DIRECTION: at 09:45 MDT's +1.09% LAGGED four of five medtech peers; at 14:21Z it LED ALL FIVE and XLV; at 15:22Z it LEADS THREE AND TRAILS TWO - ABT +2.86% and BSX +2.50% against MDT +2.30%, with BDX +1.72%, ZBH +1.64%, XLV +0.88% and SPY +0.53% behind. XLV is flat hour-over-hour at 0.89 to 0.88, so the firming was medtech-specific rather than broad healthcare, and the 10:21 claim that the sector component had drained out entirely is NARROWED: it rotated rather than drained. The alpha reading survives where the entry actually pre-registered it - MDT is 4.3x SPY and 2.6x XLV - but no longer against the subgroup, which makes the OPEN's honest beta caveat closer to true than the mid-session's correction of it. THE MARKETABILITY GAP WIDENED FOR A SECOND HOUR and is still recorded rather than repaired: 93.07 rested 0.86% under the bid at 10:21 and rests 1.09 or 1.16% under it now, so the order struck AT the offer is further into being the pullback limit its own text said it was not taking. IT IS NOT RAISED - the 2026-08-18 rule says widening the time was never permission to widen the price. FILL WINDOW RE-MEASURED: 93.07 was reachable in the 13:45Z strike bar (low 92.510) and the 13:50Z bar (low 92.845) and has NOT been touched since, every bar from 13:55Z having a low of 93.34 or higher - EIGHTY-SEVEN MINUTES untouched against thirty last hour, with the closest approach a 93.340 low in the 14:35Z bar, 0.29% clear. The level was correct and immediately fillable for about ten minutes; what is missing is execution.
entryWatch.why: The primary case is the day-2 structure off a beat AND raise, not the cohort. That ordering is deliberate: yesterday's DG entry rested on a cohort-laggard framing that inverted by 14:22 while the spec sat unfilled, so the sympathy-laggard reading is available here but is written down as a secondary tailwind rather than the load-bearing claim. Also recorded before the outcome: eight price-target raises landed in one pre-market (Mizuho 100-115, Leerink 104-111, Evercore 105-106, Wells Fargo 102-104, Baird 91-100, Truist 86-99, Stifel 80-95, Jefferies 88-95) with a mean target of 101.74 - which sits BELOW the mechanical +20% take-profit at 111.68. This trade most likely closes on the time stop rather than the target, and it says so at entry rather than discovering it at the retro.

entryWatch.why: Kept as the standing example. The spec died VALID rather than wrong - none of its three invalidations fired - and it still did not fill, because it was struck 0.38% under the bid of a name that rose on every bar. Today's MDT entry is struck AT the offer for that reason, and this row is what that decision is answering.

entryWatch.why: This is the row MDT is graded against. Same shape at the start - a large beat, a gap, a fade - and opposite resolutions: SAIC lost its pre-print close on day 2 and MDT held 1.53% above it. The rulebook has no rule that says 'a big beat is a buy'; it has a rule about what the tape does with the gap, and these two names are the worked example of why.
